projects.title: Uncle Boojie’s
projects.headline: Five pages, five ways to make content easier to read
projects.tagline: An editorial page, a long historical post, an eleven-chapter document, the Experience page and a cocktail recipe book — each needed its own answer.
projects.summary: Five pages for a bar website, each with a different kind of content.
description: During my internship at Andrew Kung Group, I designed five pages for Uncle Boojie’s website. Each one had a different kind of content, and each one needed its own answer to the same question: how do I make this content easier to read, follow and act on?

On desktop, a side menu keeps all eleven chapters of a long document one click away; on mobile, the same chapters become an accordion. The Experience page became a card system with a request form that fills itself in.
I worked only with the client’s existing text, documented every decision, and presented versions for approval before building the final one.
projects.caption: The Uncle Boojie’s website, designed and built in WordPress (Divi) within the site’s existing visual style.
